title: Positive root planes are Weyl conjugate to standard rank-two subsystems
statement:
Let $(M,\Phi,M^\vee,\Phi^\vee,\Delta)$ be a finite reduced based root datum with the lattice, pairing, reflection and base axioms of [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. Write $V=M\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, for $c\in\Phi$ write $s_c(v)=v-\langle v,c^\vee\rangle c$, let $W$ be the subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbf Q}(V)$ generated by the simple reflections $s_d$ with $d\in\Delta$, and put $\Phi^+=\Phi\cap\sum_{d\in\Delta}\mathbf Z_{\geq0}d$. Let $\ell:V\to\mathbf Q$ be a linear functional nonzero on every root, put $\Sigma=\{c\in\Phi:\ell(c)>0\}$, and let $a,b\in\Sigma$ be linearly independent over $\mathbf Q$. For $L=\mathbf Qa+\mathbf Qb$ there are distinct $\alpha,\beta\in\Delta$ and $w\in W$, that is, a finite product of simple reflections, such that
$$w(\Phi\cap L)=\Phi\cap(\mathbf Q\alpha+\mathbf Q\beta),\qquad w(\Sigma\cap L)=\Phi^+\cap(\mathbf Q\alpha+\mathbf Q\beta).$$
The latter set is exactly $\Phi\cap\{i\alpha+j\beta:i,j\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0},\ i+j>0\}$. No spanning assumption on $\Phi\subset V$ is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 6.2.1 proof and Lemma 6.2.3, printed pp.199--200: reduction of arbitrary same-sign root pairs to a simple rank-two subsystem. Root-plane/chamber formulation of the root-system input; formulated by the agent. Read online; archival literature copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this reductive/root-system result.

proof.text: Put $E=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf Q}\Phi\subseteq V$. The base axiom of [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization] makes $\Delta$ a rational basis of $E$. Work first in $E_{\mathbf R}=E\otimes_{\mathbf Q}\mathbf R$. The root and reflection formulas extend there; each reflection permutes $\Phi$, and its root-coroot values on roots are integers. Rational vectors proportional over $\mathbf R$ are proportional over $\mathbf Q$ (compute the scalar from any nonzero rational coordinate), so the reducedness axiom still holds. The group $H$ generated by these extended root reflections injects into the permutations of $\Phi$: an element fixing every root fixes their real span. Thus $H$ is finite. Choose Euclidean coordinates on $E_{\mathbf R}$ and set $B(x,y)=\sum_{h\in H}(hx,hy)_0$. This form is positive definite (the identity summand is positive on every nonzero vector) and $H$-invariant (right multiplication permutes the summands).

source.place: Appendix C.12--C.20, printed pp.610--611; explicit restriction to the root span and finite averaging

proof.text: For each root $c$, invariance gives $B(s_cx,s_cc)=B(x,c)$, while $s_cc=-c$ and $s_cx=x-\langle x,c^\vee\rangle c$. Therefore $-B(x,c)+\langle x,c^\vee\rangle B(c,c)=B(x,c)$, so $\langle x,c^\vee\rangle=2B(x,c)/B(c,c)$. The extended reflections are exactly the orthogonal reflections for $B$. Consequently $\Phi$ in $E_{\mathbf R}$ satisfies all the spanning, finiteness, reducedness and crystallographic hypotheses of the Euclidean chamber and reflection-generation lemmas used below.

source.place: Appendix C.19--C.20, printed p.611; direct computation of the orthogonal-reflection formula

proof.text: Choose a rational functional $f:E\to\mathbf Q$ vanishing on $L$ but on no root outside $L$. Here is the finite avoidance argument, including the case $E=L$. For each $c\in\Phi\setminus L$, evaluation at $c+L\ne0$ is a nonzero linear form on $(E/L)^*$. Finitely many nonzero linear forms admit a common nonzero value: induct on their number, having chosen $u$ avoiding the first $n-1$, choose $v$ on which the last is nonzero; each equation $\lambda_i(u+t v)=0$ excludes at most one rational $t$, so choose $t$ outside this finite list. With no roots outside $L$, take $f=0$. Extend $f$ and $\ell|_E$ to $E_{\mathbf R}$. Choose a positive rational $\epsilon$ with $\epsilon |\ell(c)|<|f(c)|$ for every root outside $L$ (a finite set of positive bounds). Put $g=f+\epsilon\ell$. Then $g$ is nonzero on every root; off $L$ its sign is that of $f$, and on $L$ its sign is that of $\ell$.

source.place: Appendix C.9 and C.21--C.22, printed pp.609,612; agent-supplied finite avoidance and chamber perturbation

proof.text: The positive definite form identifies $E_{\mathbf R}$ with its dual: its matrix is invertible, since a kernel vector would satisfy $B(x,x)=0$. Thus write $g(x)=B(t,x)$. Since $g$ is nonzero on every root, $t$ lies in a chamber. Apply the base/chamber correspondence and its sign clause in [lem-sfb-root-chamber-simple-transitivity] to obtain a base $D\subset\Phi$ with $\{c\in\Phi:g(c)>0\}=\Phi\cap\sum_{d\in D}\mathbf Z_{\geq0}d$. This is the base of the perturbed chamber, not a base chosen only for the subsystem.

source.place: Appendix C.9--C.10, printed pp.609--610, and C.21--C.22, printed p.612; base of the perturbed chamber

proof.text: Set $J=D\cap L$. Every $d\in D$ has $g(d)>0$; hence $f(d)\geq0$, with equality exactly for $d\in J$, by the sign control in step 3. Express any root $c\in\Phi\cap L$ or its negative as $\sum_{d\in D}n_d d$, $n_d\geq0$. Applying $f$ gives $0=\sum n_d f(d)$, so $n_d=0$ outside $J$. In particular the independent roots $a,b$ belong to $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf Q}J$. Since $J\subset L$ and $D$ is independent, $J$ has exactly two elements, say $u,v$, and $L=\mathbf Qu+\mathbf Qv$. The sign clause for $D$, together with $g|_L=\epsilon\ell|_L$, now gives $\Sigma\cap L=\Phi\cap\{iu+jv:i,j\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0},\ i+j>0\}$.

source.place: Appendix C.21--C.22, printed p.612; explicit nonnegative-coordinate face argument

proof.text: The rational base $\Delta$ is also a real base of $E_{\mathbf R}$. By equivariance and transitivity in [lem-sfb-root-chamber-simple-transitivity], some $h\in H$ sends $D$ to $\Delta$. Apply [lem-sfb-simple-root-reflection-generation] with the base $\Delta$ to express $h$ as a finite product $s_{d_1}\cdots s_{d_k}$ with $d_i\in\Delta$. Let $w=s_{d_1}\cdots s_{d_k}$ be the same product of the original rational automorphisms of $V$. Then $w\in W$, its restriction to $E$ agrees with $h$ on the roots, and it permutes $\Phi$. Put $\alpha=w(u)$ and $\beta=w(v)$. These are distinct elements of $\Delta$, and $w(L)=\mathbf Q\alpha+\mathbf Q\beta$.

source.place: Appendix C.10--C.11, printed p.610, and C.22, printed p.612; Weyl transport of bases and its lift to V

proof.text: Because $w$ is bijective and permutes $\Phi$, $w(\Phi\cap L)=\Phi\cap w(L)$. Applying $w$ to the last equality of step 5 gives $w(\Sigma\cap L)=\Phi\cap\{i\alpha+j\beta:i,j\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0},\ i+j>0\}$. Finally, uniqueness of coordinates in the independent base $\Delta$ says that a root in $\mathbf Q\alpha+\mathbf Q\beta$ has zero coordinates on all other simple roots; its membership in $\Phi^+$ is therefore exactly that its $\alpha,\beta$ coordinates are nonnegative integers. The zero pair is excluded because roots are nonzero. These are both required equalities and the asserted final description. All arguments took place in the root span until the explicit lift in step 6, so no spanning assumption on $\Phi\subset V$ was added.

source.place: Appendix C.21--C.22, printed p.612; coordinate description after transport

proof_origin.place: Appendix C.9--C.11, C.19--C.22, printed pp.609--612; explicit root-plane face argument supplementing the chamber theory. Conrad Theorem 6.2.1 proof, printed p.200, motivates the application.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NU-ea84d684b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery. It changes only the item lem-sfb-root-plane-positive-parabolic (unsplit to split, 7 steps) and adds a report. It creates no new nodes, edits no units and declares no tool_uses. There is no repair note for this item, so it is an ordinary first split, not a 2026-10-21 re-split. The statement is unchanged and true: it is the rank-two case of the standard fact (Bourbaki VI 1.7) that Phi meet any subspace is Weyl-conjugate to a standard parabolic subsystem, together with its positive system. I tested it on rank 2 (E=L, f=0), A1xA1, B2 with the orthogonal long roots e1+e2 and e1-e2 (the short roots are kept), B3 with L=span(e1+e2,e1-e2) (gives the parabolic {e2-e3,e3}), G2 with two long roots (the whole G2, not just A2), and a central part of M (no spanning assumption). Step checks: step 1 restricts to the root span E, where Delta is a basis, keeps reducedness over R, makes H finite through its faithful action on Phi, and averages a form (Milne C.15-C.19, pp.610-611). Step 2 derives the orthogonal-reflection formula from invariance (C.20). Step 3 writes out the finite avoidance over Q and the epsilon perturbation g=f+eps*l, with the correct signs off L and on L. Step 4 uses the base/chamber bijection and the sign clause from the statement (not the proof) of lem-sfb-root-chamber-simple-transitivity. Step 5 is the face argument: f is nonnegative on D and vanishes exactly on J=D meet L, so J has two elements and Sigma meet L is the cone on u,v. Step 6 gets h with hD=Delta from simple transitivity, equivariance and injectivity, writes h as a word in simple reflections with lem-sfb-simple-root-reflection-generation applied to Delta, and lifts the word to w in W acting on V. Step 7 transports and uses uniqueness of Delta-coordinates. All three cited nodes are in the item's unit sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability. The Milne App. C sources check out at the cited places: C.9 p.609, C.10-C.11 p.610, C.21-C.22 p.612. proof_origin is agent, which is correct for the face argument, and no SGA is used. The citer, lem-sfb-full-root-hom-extension step 2, uses exactly Xi = Phi meet L meet Sigma and a simple-reflection word. The 11 Mathlib searches cover LeanSearch, Loogle, LeanFinder and grep, and none found the result. No changes.
